citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering seven types of mathematical reasoning and diverse visual contexts including geometry diagrams, charts, natural images, and scientific figures.
name: MathVista
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 independent annotations per item for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling and for the three new datasets. For human performance baseline on testmini, each question was assigned to 5 annotators.
rai:annotatorDemographics: For the three new datasets: graduate students in STEM fields. For VQA mathematical reasoning labeling: expert annotators (details not specified beyond expertise). For human performance baseline (AMT): workers with a history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks and an acceptance score higher than 0.99, required to have a high school diploma or higher. Workers were compensated at $18 per hour for the Multimodal Bard assessment task.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling: Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial consistency among three annotators. For the three new datasets: inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% (only 6 out of 736 questions had disagreements). For mathematical reasoning category annotation: 94.1% of examples had exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations; 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in paper figures). Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for human performance baseline evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-step annotation process: (1) For VQA mathematical reasoning labeling: three expert annotators independently labeled examples using a custom annotation tool with instructions defining mathematical problems (involving numbers/symbols requiring operations, or complex reasoning including logical/abstract/pattern reasoning). Annotators chose Yes/No/Unsure and could leave comments. (2) For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA): all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency. Disagreements (6 out of 736 questions) were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. (3) Mathematical reasoning category labeling: expert annotators manually labeled reasoning categories from seven candidates for 1,000 examples using a dedicated annotation tool.
rai:dataBiases: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. A sampling strategy was used for testmini to maintain distribution closely resembling the whole set (KL Divergence of 0.008 and Total Variation distance of 0.035). The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions (Chinese and Persian), reflecting multilingual content. The benchmark includes varying grade levels (elementary, high school, college) to avoid bias toward a single difficulty level. Human performance baseline required high school diploma or higher given that 30.9% of problems are high-school level and 10.8% are college-level.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected from three sources: (1) Nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings (2,666 examples), including GPS, MWP, and TQA datasets; (2) 19 general VQA datasets (2,739 examples) selected from over 70 reviewed datasets that contain math-related instances and are publicly available; (3) Three newly annotated datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) with 736 examples created to address gaps in logical reasoning on puzzle test figures, algebraic reasoning over functional plots, and scientific reasoning with academic paper figures. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of: (1) 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets); (2) Puzzle test figures from online learning platforms (IQTest); (3) Functional plots for algebraic reasoning (FunctionQA); (4) Academic paper figures including tables, figures, and charts from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface (PaperQA). Annotations such as solutions, programs, parsing results, and grounded theorems were also collected from source datasets.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. The overall dataset was compiled and released alongside the ICLR 2024 paper.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains (science, college-level math) makes data collection labor-intensive, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneous sources; annotations lack unified format and structure (e.g., logic forms from Geometry3K, natural language solutions from TabMWP, theorems from TheoremQA). The benchmark focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models at time of publication. The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions (Chinese and Persian), which may affect model performance evaluation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words (e.g., most, least, mean, average, total, sum, percentage, ratio, fraction) were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Three expert annotators then manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples. Metadata annotations (question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context) were obtained from source dataset details. Mathematical reasoning categories were automatically annotated and verified by expert annotators for 1,000 examples (94.1% exact match rate).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets (e.g., refining potential data noise) in response to community feedback, and to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MathVista is designed to advance AI capabilities in mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, with applications in educational disciplines, logical queries about statistical data, and theorem proving and scientific discovery. The benchmark highlights a significant gap (10.4%) between the best AI model (GPT-4V) and human performance, underscoring the need for further development of general-purpose AI agents. The benchmark can guide future foundation model design to address failure modes such as hallucination and incorrect calculations.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of LLMs and LMMs in visual contexts; benchmarking foundation models on tasks requiring fine-grained visual understanding and compositional reasoning; facilitating development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios; model development validation (testmini subset); standard evaluation (test subset with online evaluation platform). Intended for evaluating AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor in the evaluation pipeline, achieving more than 99.5% accuracy on 200 examples. EasyOCR (JaidedAI, 2020) was used to detect OCR text from images for augmented LLM experiments. Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions for augmented LLM experiments. Heuristic rules with a dictionary of quantity words were used for automatic selection of mathematical problems from VQA datasets.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling such as cloud filtering, incomplete records, or unavailable observations in the dataset collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; the dataset consists of question-answer pairs and images without missing value imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, resampling, synthetic insertion) is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of mathematical reasoning questions with images; no personal or sensitive information is collected about individuals, though some natural images may contain people (e.g., celebrity age questions).
null_reasons.license: No license is explicitly stated in the paper.
